caveats: Parses, never repairs (mzLib's rule): an accession outside the UniProt and RefSeq protein grammars is unrecognized and kept verbatim, entry_accession equal to input. That includes lower case, surrounding spaces, a FASTA header (sp|P04637|P53_HUMAN), a decoy, contaminant or entrapment prefix (DECOY_P04637), and ProteinDbLoader's collision counter (P04637_2, which names a different entry whose accession collided).

entry_accession names the entry, not a sequence: P04637 and P04637-2 share it but are different sequences, and the isoform UniProt displays for an entry can carry any number. It answers 'same entry', never 'same sequence'.
A protein-group accession joined with '|' (P04637|P02768) is unrecognized as a whole: mzLib does not split it. Split protein groups first.
Only RefSeq protein accessions (NP_, XP_, YP_, WP_, AP_) are recognized; a RefSeq transcript (NM_) or an Ensembl id (ENSP...) is unrecognized.

A variant suffix is read only after an entry mzLib recognizes, in the form mzLib's GetAccession writes: '_', the original residues, a 1-based position, the variant residues (S70N; a deletion A80; a stop gain Q5*), repeated for several (S70N_A80T). applied_variants is that suffix as written: it is not checked against any sequence.
An isoform or version number too large for a 32-bit integer (over 2147483647) reads as null while the accession still counts as UniProt or RefSeq: mzLib keeps the entry and drops the number.
Each stdin line is one accession, given to mzLib exactly as read; blank lines are skipped. One row per line, in input order, duplicates included.
